steps.message:
# Correct support contract entitlements

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service and keeps its procedures in the `docs` service. You can use both through the MCP servers of the same names.

Every support ticket should carry the priority, response target and tags that its account's support contract entitles it to. Some do not: contracts have been upgraded, downgraded or have lapsed, and some accounts are covered through a parent account. Check every ticket of team `support` with status `open` or `pending` against the current support contract entitlements in the docs and the documents they point to, as of now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC. The docs service also keeps older revisions; use only the ones in force.

The tickets service does not let you edit priorities or labels. The desk records an entitlement correction as a comment, and a nightly sync applies it to the ticket.

1. Add exactly one comment to each ticket that needs a correction, with the text `Entitlement: <priority> <labels>`, where `<priority>` is the ticket's entitled priority and `<labels>` is the complete set of entitlement labels the ticket should carry, in alphabetical order, separated by single spaces.
2. Create one report ticket:
   - title: `Contract tier corrections 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P3`
   - labels: `entitlements`
   - body: one line per ticket you commented on, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <account> <tier>`, where `<account>` is the account id exactly as the ticket's `Account:` line writes it, or `none` when the ticket has no such line, and `<tier>` is the tier the account has now, and nothing else

Do not change the status of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"support-contracts","title":"Support contract entitlements","tags":["contracts","support"],"updated_at":"2026-09-01","body":"# Support contract entitlements

Status: current. Revision 2026-09, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces support-contracts-2025. Account tiers come from doc contract-register, revision 2026-09.

The intake form writes the customer's answers as lines at the top of each ticket body. The lines that count here are `Account:` and `Impact:`. The title, the free text and the customer's email address are the customer's own words and never decide the account, the tier or the impact. A ticket without an `Impact:` line has impact normal.

## The tier of an account

Tiers from lowest to highest: basic, silver, gold, platinum.

1. Look the account up in doc contract-register; account ids match ignoring case. An account that is not in the register, and a ticket without an `Account:` line, have tier basic.
2. A row's tier is in force from 00:00 UTC on its effective date. Before that date the account has the tier in the Previous tier column, where `-` means no contract.
3. A contract covers the account up to and including its end date; `-` means no end date. From the day after the end date the contract has lapsed, and the account has no contract of its own.
4. An account with no contract of its own has tier basic, unless rule 5 gives it more.
5. An account with a parent account has the higher of its own tier and its parent's tier, where the parent's tier is found with these same rules, so a grandparent counts too. A parent whose contract has lapsed passes on only what it has through its own parent.

Tiers apply as of now: a ticket opened under an older contract still gets the entitlements of the tier its account has today.

## Entitlements

The tier and the ticket's impact give the priority.

| Impact | basic | silver | gold | platinum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| critical | P2 | P1 | P1 | P1 |
| high | P3 | P2 | P2 | P1 |
| normal | P4 | P3 | P3 | P2 |
| low | P4 | P4 | P4 | P3 |

The tier and that priority give the response target, in hours to the first response.

| Priority | basic | silver | gold | platinum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | - | 4 | 2 | 1 |
| P2 | 24 | 8 | 4 | 2 |
| P3 | 48 | 24 | 8 | 4 |
| P4 | 72 | 48 | 24 | 8 |

The tier gives the tags.

| Tier | Tags |
|---|---|
| basic | tier/basic |
| silver | tier/silver |
| gold | tier/gold |
| platinum | named-engineer, tier/platinum |

## Corrections

A ticket shows its priority in the priority field, its response target as the label `response/<hours>h`, and its tags as labels. The entitlement labels of a ticket are its labels that start with `response/` or `tier/`, and `named-engineer`. Other labels are not entitlement labels and play no part here.

A ticket needs a correction when its priority differs from the entitled priority, or when its entitlement labels are not exactly the entitled response label and the entitled tags, no more and no fewer.
"}

Checking the remaining tickets against their tiers: 1312 and 1316 are both silver critical tickets that need P1 and a 4h response, and 1313 is a basic high-priority ticket that should be P3 at 48h. Ticket 1314 also needs P1, while 1310 should drop to P2.

Checking the rest of the tickets against their tiers: 1324 is platinum low-priority, so it should be P3 at 4h, and 1325 is a basic critical ticket that should be P2 at 24h. Ticket 1326 is silver normal at P3 and 24h, 1328 is silver with no impact at P3 and 24h, and 1329 is gold normal at P3 and 8h, which already matches. Ticket 1330 is gold high-priority and should be P2 at 4h.

I'm going through the last batch of tickets against their tiers. Ticket 1335 on 2106 is platinum high-priority, so it should be P1 at 1h with a named engineer, and 1336 on 2403 is platinum low-priority that needs P3 at 4h. Ticket 1337 on the basic-tier 2204 should be P3 at 48h, and 1339 on 2403 needs P2 at 2h.

I'm going through the remaining ticket corrections, confirming each of the last few tickets matches its account tier, and then tallying the list of 22 tickets that need changing.

I'm now going through the tier assignments for the last few accounts and tickets, confirming the tier labels for each one and tallying the corrections I've already identified.

The tickets I commented on are #1302, #1306, #1307, #1310, #1312, #1313, #1314, #1316–#1319, #1321, #1323–#1326, #1328, #1330, #1335–#1337 and #1339.
